clue.text: Fell over in den

parts.note: a fell is an animal's skin or pelt, so a hide
over means finished, out

explanation.surface: Someone takes a tumble inside a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past tense of fall, but here it is the noun for an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a secret retreat or lair where one lies low, a synonym.

clue.text: Fence affording uninterrupted view of two hectares

indicators.note: two asks for the abbreviation that follows to be written down a second time

parts.note: HA is the abbreviation for hectare

explanation.surface: A landowner's sunken boundary leaves the vista over a small estate open.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch-and-wall boundary on English country estates, invisible from the house so the view runs on.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha-ha is a sunken barrier that keeps livestock out without blocking the landscape, so it is a kind of hidden boundary.

clue.text: Demand money to dine out in City

parts.note: to dun someone is to press them for payment of a debt

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of dine are thrown out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A creditor chases payment before going for a meal in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes INED from DINE; Dunedin is a city in New Zealand's South Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunedin is a city in Otago, New Zealand, an example of the class.

clue.text: Orders English stout

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire, so orders become OBES

explanation.surface: Someone asks for an English dark beer at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orders' and 'stout' suggest a pub, but stout is the adjective meaning fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout as an adjective describes a heavily built, fat person, a synonym.

clue.text: Conducts class to gain promotion legally

parts.note: to take a class or a group somewhere is to conduct it
ilk means sort or class

explanation.surface: A teacher leads lessons in the hope of advancement at a law school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a barrister who becomes a Queen's or King's Counsel is said to take silk, from the silk gown worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming senior counsel is the barrister's promotion, named after the silk gown it brings.

clue.text: Martyr's protector abandoned by Henry

indicators.note: abandoned by says one letter walks out of the longer word and leaves it

parts.note: a champion defends or protects a cause or person
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A saint's defender is deserted by a king called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Martyr's' is read as 'Martyr is': Edmund Campion was a Jesuit martyred under Elizabeth I. 'Henry' suggests a king but is the physics unit H.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Edmund Campion was an English Jesuit executed in 1581 and venerated as a Catholic martyr.

clue.text: Resigning for fixing the draw, it is reported

indicators.note: it is reported means we take the word as it would be heard spoken

parts.note: seeding a tournament fixes the draw so top players meet late

explanation.surface: A player quits over a rigged tournament draw, rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceding is yielding or giving up, so resigning a position or right.

clue.text: Early drop-outs in young set

parts.note: a child's first set of teeth all fall out early, the 'drop-outs' of a young mouth

explanation.surface: Youngsters quitting school early among the trendy young crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Children lose their first teeth young, so these are the first things to drop from a youthful set.

clue.text: Vile drunk elbowing wife aside

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering about into a new order
aside says the named letter is pushed out of the word

explanation.surface: A nasty drunk shoves his wife out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aside' removes W from ELBOWING to leave ELBOING, which 'drunk' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means base or dishonourable, so a synonym for vile.

clue.text: Plant grower has room for little ones on island

parts.note: a nursery is a room for small children
Man is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A gardener has a children's playroom in his island house.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurseryman raises young plants for sale, so is a horticultural grower.

clue.text: Harassed by the beak?

definitions.meaning: nagged or bossed about, usually by a wife
read literally, pecked by a hen's beak

explanation.definitionFit: Being henpecked is being nagged; literally it is being pecked by a hen's beak.

clue.text: Protective cover for a Queen, say

definitions.meaning: a lining or sleeve that protects something
the Queen Mary and Queen Elizabeth were famous ocean passenger ships

explanation.definitionFit: A liner is both an inner covering and a large passenger ship, the Queen Mary being one example.

clue.text: Place of reflection for women wanting to keep up appearances

definitions.text: Place of reflection for women wanting to keep up appearances

parts.words: Place of reflection for women wanting to keep up appearances
parts.note: reflection means a mirror image, not thought; the furniture has a mirror for making up

explanation.surface: A quiet spot where image-conscious women come to think.
explanation.definitionFit: This bedroom furniture has a mirror before which people make up and groom themselves.

clue.text: Liberal in a publication, a friend and ally

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for a publication

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a publication
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A Liberal writing in a magazine names a friend and political partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to join or combine forces, so to merge into one.

clue.text: Chamber with ways in and out serving various functions

definitions.text: Chamber with ways in and out
definitions.meaning: an engine pipe chamber with several openings, as in an exhaust part
having many forms or uses, many-sided

explanation.definitionFit: An engine's multi-port pipe has this name, and as an adjective the word means many and varied.

clue.text: Windy apartment university temporarily provided

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
lent means given on loan, provided for a time

explanation.surface: A gusty flat that a university has loaned out for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatulent means suffering from gas in the gut, which is windy in the digestive sense.

clue.text: First sign of moisture in piping needed treatment

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for piping

parts.note: a piping voice is high and thin, reedy

indicators.note: First sign of points to the opening letter of the word moisture

explanation.surface: Damp in the pipes needs fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a cure or treatment for an ailment or problem, a synonym.

clue.text: Inspecting camouflaged sniper with sawn-off gun

indicators.note: camouflaged suggests the letters are disguised in a new arrangement
sawn-off says the word has its tail cut away

explanation.surface: A hidden marksman with a shortened shotgun scans the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sawn-off' cuts N from GUN to give GU, which joins SNIPER for 'camouflaged' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Perusing means reading or examining carefully, so inspecting.

clue.text: Record crowd producing standstill

parts.note: a log is a written record
to jam is to crowd or cram together

explanation.surface: A record-breaking crowd brings everything to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a blockage or deadlock where nothing can move, so a standstill.

clue.text: Most college entertainments appear in the end rather vulgar

indicators.note: Most means all but the final letter of the following word

parts.note: a gaudy is a celebratory dinner for old members at an Oxford college

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of appear

explanation.surface: Most college parties turn out somewhat tasteless in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaudier is the comparative of gaudy, garish and showy, so somewhat more vulgar.

clue.text: Get out the beads in chapel

indicators.note: Get out suggests the letters are taken apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unpacks a rosary during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Bethesda, a biblical pool, became a common name for Welsh nonconformist chapels.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethesda is a name often given to nonconformist places of worship, so a chapel by name.

clue.text: Clutch of eggs from this sort of duck?

definitions.meaning: the eggs a bird sits on at one time
a ... duck is an easy target

explanation.definitionFit: A sitting is a batch of eggs being brooded, and a sitting duck is a helpless target.

clue.text: Winner with 24, none the less leaving a sour taste in the mouth

definitions.text: leaving a sour taste in the mouth

parts.note: an ace is a winning serve or card, a winner

indicators.note: less says the following item is subtracted from the other word

parts.note: 24 refers to the answer at 24-down, OTIC
O is nil, zero, none

explanation.surface: A winner none the less leaves a bitter aftertaste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'none the less' looks like a stock phrase; 'none' is O, and 'less' removes it from 24-down's answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic means like vinegar, so sour-tasting.

clue.text: One adept at picking holes in people?

definitions.text: One adept at picking holes in people?

parts.words: One adept at picking holes in people?
parts.note: picking holes usually means faultfinding, but here someone literally pierces people with needles

explanation.surface: A habitual critic who finds fault with everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: This therapist inserts fine needles into the skin, quite literally making holes in patients.

clue.text: Imagines this insect and others like it

definitions.text: Imagines this insect and others like it

parts.words: Imagines this insect and others like it
parts.note: Imagines is not a verb but a plural noun: several adult insects in their final form

explanation.surface: Someone pictures a bug and its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the adult winged stage of an insect, and its Latin plural is imagines.

clue.text: Noticed part of organ near temple

indicators.note: part says only a piece of the word Noticed is used

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a section of the organ beside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' and 'temple' suggest a church, but the organ is the ear, next to the temple of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the anatomical adjective for the ear, which sits beside the temple of the head.

clue.text: A part that's inaudible on stage

definitions.text: A part that's inaudible on stage

parts.words: A part that's inaudible on stage
parts.note: a speech the other characters supposedly cannot hear, though the audience can

explanation.surface: An actor's role nobody in the theatre can hear.
explanation.definitionFit: This stage remark is spoken to the audience and treated as unheard by the other characters.

clue.text: Person with family values almost sad going round the island

indicators.note: going round says the shortened word wraps around the island
almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: triste is a literary word for sad
Bali is an Indonesian island

explanation.surface: A homely type is nearly miserable while touring an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Triste is an old literary borrowing from French for sad; 'almost' drops its final E and 'going round' wraps what is left around the Indonesian island.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribalist puts loyalty to clan or kin first, so values the extended family group.

clue.text: Misjudge a contraction as irregular

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake, misjudge
a tic is an involuntary muscle contraction

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly thinks a shortened word is nonstandard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contraction' suggests a shortened word like don't, but it is a muscle twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means unpredictable and uneven, a synonym.

clue.text: So-called farmer mostly in charge of rural affairs

indicators.note: mostly means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: George comes from the Greek for farmer, so a farmer by name

explanation.surface: A man dubbed a farmer largely runs the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgic, as in Virgil's Georgics, describes poetry about farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgic means relating to agriculture and the countryside.
